notes.title: Build InDev 17b Stable Released
notes.content:
InDev 17b is here! 17b adds a few new requested features, some bug fixes and some additions that didn't quite make the deadline for InDev 17's release. Hope you all enjoy!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 17b Stable Change Log
- Mini map moved to a drop down tab, so you can now view the minimap without leaving the game world.
- Map scrolling bound limits set to +- 256 pixels of the original map size, formally +-128.
- The map slowdown effect doesnt "stick" along edges anymore, causing weird behaviors if you zoom in and out after hitting a map's edge.
- Removed the interface scaling setting.
- You can now pause the game with spacebar.
- Map movement speed when using WASD or the mouse now varies depending on the map's zoom level. In general, you scroll slower the closer you are zoomed in.
- The same music track will now never play twice in a row.
- You can now interact with the tips system while the game is paused.
- The console is now visible again.
- Thunder and lightning sound effects added.
- Reduced the amount of particles on the world map.
- Readded pause and dismantle buttons to the bottom GUI, but you can still use the pause and dismantle buttons on the left hand tab as well.
- Removed some junk files our of the resource folder.

notes.title: Build InDev 17 Stable Released
notes.content:
The first stable build of 2016 has arrived! This update completely overhauls the entire game's graphics assets from scratch, quadrupling the base game resolution and doubling the animation frames for all mobs. This patch also has a plethora of under the hood changes, improving memory usage, fixing some minor bugs and making a few changes to the interface.

Also, due to the entire game being redrawn I am running another Screenshot Roundup. If you're interested, check out this announcement!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 17 Stable Change Log
- The entire game's art assets have been completely redrawn from scratch at four times the resolution.
- All animations are now 8 frames, instead of 4.
- New music tracks, "Misty Awakening" and "Unbroken Circle".
- Added a new splash screen melody.
- Track "Main Theme in Piano" has been remastered from scratch.
- The "Unassign Work" button has been removed.
- You can hold the "Accent Mode" button (Left Control by default) to unassign work for whatever work assignment is currently selected.
- Fixed building health bars, they no longer report 0% health when health drops below 10%.
- Improved particle performance slightly.
- Rewrote the way the game loads and transitions between states, improving load times and peak memory usage.
- Cullis Gate's max energy has been reduced to 250, making it able to fire more often.
- Ghosts are now twice as likely to appear.
- Fixed the positioning of the "News and Announcements" bar on the main menu in some situations.
- Increased the "Stuck" movement speed when a mob is trying to walk off of a blocked tile.
- Fixed building and population dropdowns from miscalculating what the "last page" of the list was when clicking the "bottom" button.
- Fixed some objects (Mainly walls) from being misclicked when trying to pause or dismantle them.
- New skirmish mode games now correctly center on the villagers when the game starts.

notes.title: InDev 17 Screenshot Roundup Event! Get your screenshots posted on the official store page!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! It's time for another (and possibly biggest ever) screenshot round up! Every few updates I revamp the Steam store page, adding more recent screenshots. One of my favorite things to do is to take screenshots that you guys have made. I feel they're a more personal, realistic representation of the game and it's fun to get the community involved! 

This round is very important, because I'm going to scrap the entire store page and rebuild it from the ground up using the new art assets from InDev 17. So I urge all of you to submit your coolest, best work!

If you want to submit your screenshot to the event, the higher quality the better! I'm looking for screenshots that really show off all the features of the game. These screenshots can be of anything you want, any mode, anywhere.


 Must be version InDev 17 Unstable 2 or higher! (How to access Unstable builds)
 1920x1080 resolution. 1280x720 or higher can be acceptable too, but 1920x1080 is best!
 Take them in full screen mode if you can (F10 to toggle in-game).
 You can take screenshots either with the built in in-game hotkey (F2), or with Steam's overlay hotkey (F12). If you plan on uploading them to the Steam Community Hub, F12 is probably easier.
 Upload them to the Steam Community Hub, or upload them to a image sharing service of your choosing (imgur, for example). Make sure the images are as least compressed as possible! I can't use over-compressed images.
 Post a link to your image in the comments below!


The images selected will be put up on the store page, with your username on it. If you don't want your username posted, please inform me in the comments below when submitting.

You can submit as many or as few as you like, and you can have multiplies selected. The higher quality the better!

Have fun! Looking forward to your submissions. The images selected will be posted to the store page shortly after InDev 17 Stable is released!

notes.title: Build InDev 17 Unstable 2 Released
notes.content:
Click here for help on accessing the Unstable branch!

The first patch of 2016 has arrived! The GUI has been completely redrawn, and InDev 17 Stable is just around the corner. Only a few things are left before I can push out the next stable release. For now, enjoy the brand new GUI, new music, and a few other juicy tidbits that snuck there way in to this build. :)

I'll be running another Screenshot Roundup starting sometime later today. If you want to jump the gun, take some screenshots and post them to the community hub, the best ones will be featured on the store page!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 17 Unstable 2 Change Log
- The entire GUI has been redrawn from scratch, and is now double the resolution.
- New music tracks, "Misty Awakening" and "Unbroken Circle".
- Added a new splash screen melody.
- Track "Main Theme in Piano" has been remastered from scratch.
- Fixed missing lava and water particles.
- Fixed drawing board alignment.
- The "Unassign Work" button has been removed.
- You can hold the "Accent Mode" button (Left Control by default) to unassign work for whatever work assignment is currently selected.
- Fixed building health bars, they no longer report 0% health when health drops below 10%.

InDev 17 Unstable 1 Change Log
- Completely redrawn base tile set, upgrading the graphics from 8x8 to 16x16.
- All animations are now 8 frames, instead of 4.
- Improved particle performance slightly.
- Rewrote the way the game loads and transitions between states, improving load times and peak memory usage.
- Cullis Gate's max energy has been reduced to 250, making it able to fire more often.
- Ghosts are now twice as likely to appear.
- Fixed the positioning of the "News and Announcements" bar on the main menu in some situations.
- Increased the "Stuck" movement speed when a mob is trying to walk off of a blocked tile.

Known Issues that will be resolved before the stable build
- When creating a new map in the map editor, the system tries to load a copy of the last map loaded into memory.

notes.title: InDev 17 Road Map - The Art Update.
notes.content:
For the past 4 or 5 months I've been debating a bold concept. You may of seen me on my Twitter or on the forums discussing it but I was unsure if I wanted to go through with it. Would it hurt the game? Would players like it? What will the reaction be? Well, after some continuing discussions with members of the community and a generally overwhelming positive reaction to my samples, I've finally decided to do it.

Introducing, InDev 17 - The Art Update! This update will completely redraw the entire game tileset from scratch, from 8x8 to 16x16.

I've been working on this art for about 4 or 5 days now trying to refine a new higher resolution art style while still retaining Retro-Pixel Castles charming feel we have all fell in love with. So far, I'm very pleased with the results, and I hope you are too. 

"But, wait? I thought InDev 17 was focused on adding buildings, mobs and general content?!" You're right, that was the plan. But I've come to realized that if I am going to overhaul the art, it needs to come first. If I wait until after the next major content update it will slow down overall development of the game (because I'll have to draw all the new content twice!) So I decided I should get this update out of the way first before focusing on the next major content update.

I'm sure a lot of you want to know what this all will look like. Well you're in luck! I've drawn enough artwork to make a few sample screenshots. Let me know what you think!

notes.title: InDev 17 Pre-Planning. Submit your building ideas!
notes.content:
Greetings everyone,

InDev 17 will be a very long overdue, content heavy update. My plan is to add more buildings, monsters, maps and all sorts of other general content to the game, but the primary focus will be on the village. I'd like to get a ton of new buildings added, everything else that's added will mostly be to complement them.

So, there is where you come in! I have tons of ideas for new buildings I've been sitting on, like a tavern, schools and clinics but I'd love to hear your ideas as well.

I can't promise all of these will make it into RPC during InDev 17, but this is a good laundry list of building ideas currently on the table;

A tavern - This building will be a fun place villagers can go to relax. It will boost happiness, and while in the tavern, encourage people to interact (and thus, partner up for mating)
A church - A place to boost happiness, and while it's being used you'll also get a boost to your influence bar. The more people there, the more influence you'll gain on top of the usual gain rates.
A hospital/clinic - You can assign villagers to work there and they'll become "field medics" who will run around healing fellow villagers. Later, this will also be a place pregnant villagers can go to give birth and their child will get some bonus experience for being born there, rather than at home or on the fields.
Schools - A place where children villagers can go get educated. Children will gain experience when they visit the school, so they might get to start their adulthood a few levels higher than what they were when they were born.
More towers - I'd like to get more towers added, starting with traditional Tower Defense tower types, like a slowing tower, an AOE type tower, etc. (Tower ideas would be great to hear!)
Alchemy lab - A building that can produce potions from crystals. Villagers would visit this alchemy lab and pickup potions to carry around with them to be used as needed. For example, they might keep a healing potion on them and chug it when their health is low. (Note; this requires the inventory system, and that hasn't been added yet!)
Workshops - These will basically be mini village centers, you can plop them on the map and increase your max builders beyond 32.
Store-all building of some kind - This building will allow the villagers to store overflow resources in it, it'll take any kind of resource in the game.
Farming changes - The farming buildings will be changed somewhat, your workers will be able to boost growth speed by bringing nearby water to the crops, or by tilling/caring for the soil. This will give you a reason to keep workers at your farm, since most of the time they just sort of sit there and idle until something is grown.
Guard building changes - Guard buildings will also start functioning as way-points/patrol routes, guards will walk from one guard building to another when they have nothing to do.
Resource harvesting building changes - Currently, resource harvesting buildings (Like the lumber shack) allow their workers to deliver resources from their building to construction sites, and builders from your village center are not allowed to pickup resources from them. This will change, the harvesters will no longer deliver anything to any building other than their work building, but builders will be able to pickup resources from anywhere in the village. This will encourage more efficient resource collecting, and allow refined resources to continuously produce more effectively.


While I can't add everyone's ideas, because even some really cool ideas you may have might not quite fit the final vision of the game, that doesn't mean you guys won't have some amazing ideas I never thought of! So let me hear 'em!

notes.title: Build InDev 16 Stable Released
notes.content:
I'm over-joyed and very proud to announce the long awaited, massively-big-huge InDev 16 is finally here! This one may be one of the largest updates in the history of Retro-Pixel Castles. This update introduces a new world map system, building priority system, more godlike spells, a new lighting and shadow system, more monsters, maps, and so many other fun things! It was a long road getting this update out to you guys, but it was well worth it. :)

Have fun reading the massive change log!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 16 Change Log

The World Map! A whole new way to play. The world map allows you to play on several maps at once, creating a metagame where you can share resources between the maps. Now, rather than playing on a single map and started with a random pool of villagers, you will start the game with 50 to 60 villagers and 100 to 110 resources, you can send these resources to any map on the world map. You can also steal resources (and even villagers and monsters!) from one map and put them in another. 
Limbo tab added to the game, now when you're in-game you can use the Limbo tab to bring in creatures and resources from storage, or pull them off the map and store them back in Limbo. Limbo will work on any map in the world map, and they all share the same storage pool.
When playing a World Map game you no longer start with villagers, but around 25 are teleported in as soon as you place your Village Center, assuming that you have enough villagers in Limbo. Some starting resources are also sent along with the villagers, again if you have any stored to send.
You can no longer "lose" a game when playing on the World Map. Instead, you lose when your entire world runs out of villagers. If you run out of villagers on a World Map game you can reset the map manually inside the world map, or send in more villagers and "take back" your land.
Building priority system has been added, you can now click the building drop down list on the top GUI and reorder building priorities. Higher priority buildings will be the first built, dismantled, delivered to or repaired when workers are looking for a job to do. 
The entire save system has been mostly rewritten, to allow the game to talk between save files and the world map.
The old single map play mode has been re-purposed and named "Skirmish" mode, it functions exactly like the play mode did before the world map was introduced and is not impacted by any of the changes in this patch.
Cullis Gates have been completely rewritten, they now resurrect nearby dead villagers when they are fully charged.
Ghosts are now attracted to Cullis Gates.
The "Technology" button has been removed from the main menu, it will be re-added to the World Map screen once the feature has been added to the game. 
Completely removed "Map Descriptions" from the game. 
The credits page formatting has been fixed. 
Villagers no longer carry resources on their head and forget they're there. 
(Related to above) Fixed the loading game bug related to incorrectly assigned resources being carried when the villager carrying them dies and the game is saved. 
Fixed dead mobs from resetting to the standing animation when reloading a saved game. 
Fixed the tool tip not rendering in the correct position at some zoom levels. 
Moved the InDev disclaimer to pop up before selecting a profile, and will only pop up once per game session rather than every time you try to play a game. 
Substantially improved the performance of the entire AI and Pathfinding system. Pathfinding runs about 16 times faster than previously, and most of the AI's search algorithms have also been improved greatly. This should give everyone a great boost in performance in high mob count games. 
Added "small slimes" to the game, these slimes have a lot lower overall stats, and can not split.
Regular slimes can now split more often, but only split into the new small slimes.
New monster; The fire elemental. A somewhat rare spawn, and can light your villagers and buildings on fire. Be careful! 
Added some extra information to the crash log. 
Changed how entering full screen mode works, this may resolve some issues Intel HD and Arch Linux users have been having switching to full screen, but has been untested due to not having access to either for testing. 
Added a small light source to the mouse pointer. 
Added a ton of new lighting effects to many of the spells and effects in the game. 
There's now a chance of a severe storm, with increased lightning and rain.
Nighttime is now darker.
The world is now a little darker when it rains.
New spell; Magic Torch. Will create a long lasting light source in the specified area.
New spell; Spotlight. Not as bright as a Magic Torch, but will follow your mouse around. 
Added fire particles to the SixtyGig Logo's eyes. 
Lightning bolts no longer cause the screen to shake. 
Fixed the map editor's grab tool from breaking the GUI at certain zoom levels. 
Rewrote how the game handles map and save deletion, fixing a bunch of file deletion bugs.
Profiles no longer occasionally "Corrupt" when you try to delete them. 
Fixed a bug with ultra high resolution displays (Above 1080p) incorrectly rendering the lighting box at certain zoom levels. 
Fixed a bug where resources deleted from the game would remain taking up space on the map, so no other resource could be placed there. 
Spawn caps added, now no more than 750 monsters can spawn in Survival, and no more than 100 in Peaceful.
Added colored rings below all mobs when your mouse gets near them, indicating if they're friendly or hostile.
Mobs can no longer do "0" damage when they make a successful hit.
Reduced the overall amount of blood.
Mobs can now bleed for a period of time after taking heavy damage. 
Rewrote the entire shadow system, removing the dynamic moving shadows but increasing rendering performance by about 600%. 
Removed some very old and obsolete official maps. 
Removed map CaptainCal because it is no longer compatible with RPC.
Added 11 new maps, "Greenham", "Woodhaven", "Wheatcastle", "Northoak", "Arid River", "Survival Island" (new), "Quiet Forest", "Outlands", "Gateway", "Narrow Path" and "Enchanted Shoreline". 
Updated song "Skull Hunter"
Removed song "Try Again", replaced with updated "Goodbye Retro-Sky"
Added song "Azufre" and "Lonely Sunrise".

notes.title: Build InDev 16 Unstable 7 Released

Click here for help on accessing the Unstable branch!

Unless something goes terribly wrong, this will be the last Unstable build for InDev 16. Next release should be the long awaited InDev 16 Stable! This update ties up some loose ends, cleans up some code and brings some more rendering optimizing. This update also introduces a long awaited and heavily requested feature; building prioritizing!

Please let me know if you've noticed a increase in overall performance!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 16 Unstable 7 Change Log

- Updated the world map image a bit.
- You can no longer retrigger the initial limbo spawn in when you place a village center by reloading a save before the village center is started.
- Rebalanced initial villager and resource delivery when sending your first batch of villagers and resources out of Limbo when you start a new region on the world map.
- Villagers are no longer confused when sent out of Limbo at the beginning of a new world map region.
- Added some more system information to the crash logs.
- Rewrote the entire shadow system, removing the dynamic moving shadows but increasing rendering performance by about 600%.
- Removed some very old and obsolete official maps.

- Fixed a bug where resources deleted from the game would remain taking up space on the map, so no other resource could be placed there.
- Reduced the area of effect of all Limbo spells, to give the player a little more accuracy.
- Spawn caps added, now no more than 750 monsters can spawn in Survival, and no more than 100 in Peaceful.

notes.title: InDev 16 Screenshot Roundup Event! Get your screenshots posted on the official store page!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Every few updates I revamp the Steam store page, adding more recent screenshots. One of my favorite things to do is to take screenshots that you guys have made. I feel they're a more personal, realistic representation of the game and it's fun to get the community involved! 

If you want to submit your screenshot to the event, the higher quality the better! I'm looking for screenshots that really show off all the features of the game. These screenshots can be of anything you want, any mode, anywhere.


 Must be version InDev 16 Unstable 6 or higher! (How to access Unstable builds)
 1920x1080 resolution. 1280x720 or higher can be acceptable too, but 1920x1080 is best!
 Take them in full screen mode if you can (F10 to toggle in-game).
 You can take screenshots either with the built in in-game hotkey (F2), or with Steam's overlay hotkey (F12). If you plan on uploading them to the Steam Community Hub, F12 is probably easier.
 Upload them to the Steam Community Hub, or upload them to a image sharing service of your choosing (imgur, for example). Make sure the images are as least compressed as possible! I can't use over-compressed images.
 Post a link to your image in the comments below!


The images selected will be put up on the store page, with your username on it. If you don't want your username posted, please inform me in the comments below when submitting.

You can submit as many or as few as you like, and you can have multiplies selected. The higher quality the better!

Have fun! Looking forward to your submissions. The images selected will be posted to the store page when InDev 16 Stable is released!

Now, rather than playing on a single map and started with a random pool of villagers, you will start the game with 50 to 60 villagers and 100 to 110 resources, you can send these resources to any map on the world map. You can also steal resources (and even villagers and monsters!) from one map and put them in another.

- When playing a World Map game you no longer start with villagers, but up to 25 are teleported in as soon as you place your Village Center, assuming that you have enough villagers in Limbo. Some starting resources are also sent along with the villagers, again if you have any stored to send.
- You can no longer "lose" a game when playing on the World Map. Instead, you lose when your entire world runs out of villagers. If you run out of villagers on a World Map game you can reset the map manually inside the world map, or send in more villagers and "take back" your land.
- The entire save system has been mostly rewritten, to allow the game to talk between save files and the world map.
- The old single map play mode has been re-purposed and named "Skirmish" mode, it functions exactly like the play mode did before the world map was introduced and is not impacted by any of the changes in this patch.
- The "Technology" button has been removed from the main menu, it will be re-added to the World Map screen once the feature has been added to the game.
- Added 4 new maps, Survival Island (new), Quiet Forest, Outlands and Enchanted Shoreline.
- Updated song "Skull Hunter"
- Removed song "Try Again", replaced with updated "Goodbye Retro-Sky"
- Added song "Azufre" and "Lonely Sunrise".

Known Issues that will be resolved before the stable build
- A few button icons are missing for some of the new features, like the Magic Torch, Spotlight and World Map reset button.
- The new save system can introduce a heavy load to the game on initial load.
- When you run out of villagers in the world map, the game does not "End" like it should. You will have to delete your profile, or your save folder to "reset" the game.

- New monster; The fire elemental. A somewhat rare spawn, and can light your villagers and buildings on fire. Be careful!
- Added some extra information to the crash log.
- Changed how entering full screen mode works, this may resolve some issues Intel HD and Arch Linux users have been having switching to full screen, but has been untested due to not having access to either for testing.
- Added a small light source to the mouse pointer.
- Added a ton of new lighting effects to many of the spells and effects in the game.
- There's now a chance of a severe storm, with increased lightning and rain.
- Nighttime is now darker.
- The world is now a little darker when it rains.
- New spell; Magic Torch. Will create a long lasting light source in the specified area.
- New spell; Spotlight. Not as bright as a Magic Torch, but will follow your mouse around.
- Fixed a bug where the reported version of an old Skirmish save would be "NULL" sometimes.
- Added fire particles to the SixtyGig Logo's eyes.
- Lightning bolts no longer cause the screen to shake.
- Fixed the tool tip not rendering correctly at certain zoom levels.
- Fixed the map editor's grab tool from breaking the GUI at certain zoom levels.
- Fixed a bug with ultra high resolution displays (Above 1080p) incorrectly rendering the lighting box at certain zoom levels.
- You can now manually reset the world map via the world map GUI.
- The game now warns you if you're trying to load an old version of the world map, and gives you the option to reset your save before attempting to load.
- Profile's total days survived tick now runs as the game is being played, not just tally the values when you lose.
- Rewrote how the game handles map and save deletion, fixing a bunch of file deletion bugs.
- Profiles no longer occasionally "Corrupt" when you try to delete them.

InDev 16 Unstable 4 Change Log
- Three new maps, Woodhaven, Wheatcastle and Northoak.
- Updated map Survival Island.
- Remade map Quiet Forest.
- You can now "lose" in the world map when your total villager count drops to zero, resetting the world map.

- You can now move the world map with the keyboard, rather than just the mouse. (WASD by default).
- The world map will now warn you if you're trying to play in a region from an old version of the game, much like how Skirmish mode does.
- Changed the region buttons on the world map to make them more obvious.
- The world map fades in and out when switching game modes.

InDev 16 Unstable 3 Change Log
- New map, "Aird River".
- Villagers are now correctly removed from their work buildings when teleported to Limbo.
- Fixed a crash when you lost a skirmish map.
- Villagers no longer carry resources on their head and forget they're there.
- (Related to above) Fixed the loading game bug related to incorrectly assigned resources being carried when the villager carrying them dies and the game is saved.
- World map now has little dots wandering around on it, representing monsters and villagers in the world.
- Fixed dead mobs from resetting to the standing animation when reloading a saved game.
- Fixed the tool tip not rendering in the correct position at some zoom levels.
- Added a quick view overlay to the regions on the world map.

InDev 16 Unstable 2 Change Log
- Two new maps added, "Gateway" and "Narrow Path".
- Fixed a bug causing the Drawing Board to crash on loading.
- Fixed the map list crashing when it attempted to load an empty map pack. Sometimes this caused the Skirmish and the Map Editor menus in the main menu to crash.
- Completely removed "Map Descriptions" from the game.
- The credits page formatting has been fixed.
- Added update and render culling to the particle system in the world map, increasing performance.
- You can no longer scroll beyond the bounds of the world map.
- You can no longer cast spells to take resources or creatures from Limbo if none exist to take.
- Slightly updated the World Map image.

InDev 16 Unstable 1 Change Log
- The World Map! A whole new way to play. The world map allows you to play on several maps at once, creating a metagame where you can share resources between the maps. Now, rather than playing on a single map and started with a random pool of villagers, you will start the game with 50 to 60 villagers and 100 to 110 resources, you can send these resources to any map on the world map. You can also steal resources (and even villagers and monsters!) from one map and put them in another. 
- Limbo tab added to the game, now when you're in-game you can use the Limbo tab to bring in creatures and resources from storage, or pull them off the map and store them back in Limbo. Limbo will work on any map in the world map, and they all share the same storage pool.
- When playing a World Map game you no longer start with villagers, but up to 25 are teleported in as soon as you place your Village Center, assuming that you have enough villagers in Limbo. Some starting resources are also sent along with the villagers, again if you have any stored to send.
- You can no longer "lose" a game when playing on the World Map. Instead, you lose when your entire world runs out of villagers. If you run out of villagers on a World Map game you can reset the map manually inside the world map, or send in more villagers and "take back" your land.
- The entire save system has been mostly rewritten, to allow the game to talk between save files and the world map.
- The old single map play mode has been re-purposed and named "Skirmish" mode, it functions exactly like the play mode did before the world map was introduced and is not impacted by any of the changes in this patch.
- The "Technology" button has been removed from the main menu, it will be re-added to the World Map screen once the feature has been added to the game.
- Added 4 new maps, Survival Island (new), Quiet Forest, Outlands and Enchanted Shoreline.
- Updated song "Skull Hunter"
- Removed song "Try Again", replaced with updated "Goodbye Retro-Sky"
- Added song "Azufre" and "Lonely Sunrise".

Known Issues that will be resolved before the stable build
- A few button icons are missing for some of the new features, like the Magic Torch, Spotlight and World Map reset button.
- The new save system can introduce a heavy load to the game on initial load.
- When you run out of villagers in the world map, the game does not "End" like it should. You will have to delete your profile, or your save folder to "reset" the game.

notes.title: Build InDev 16 Unstable 1 Released
notes.content:
Click here for help on accessing the Unstable branch!

After what feels like an eternity of coding and drawing, I'm proud to announce the release of InDev 16 Unstable 1! This update welcome in the long awaited world map. It's a bit slim on content right now with only 4 maps available, but it gets the job done well enough for you guys to try it out while I continue to flesh out the new system. The next few unstable builds I'll be fixing the bugs that will no doubt creep up, refine the new mechanics, and add several new maps to play on. You're in for a hell of a new experience, I hope you enjoy it! Good luck!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 16 Unstable 1 Change Log
- The World Map! A whole new way to play. The world map allows you to play on several maps at once, creating a metagame where you can share resources between the maps. Now, rather than playing on a single map and started with a random pool of villagers, you will start the game with 50 to 60 villagers and 100 to 110 resources, you can send these resources to any map on the world map. You can also steal resources (and even villagers and monsters!) from one map and put them in another. 
- Limbo tab added to the game, now when you're in-game you can use the Limbo tab to bring in creatures and resources from storage, or pull them off the map and store them back in Limbo. Limbo will work on any map in the world map, and they all share the same storage pool.
- When playing a World Map game you no longer start with villagers, but up to 25 are teleported in as soon as you place your Village Center, assuming that you have enough villagers in Limbo. Some starting resources are also sent along with the villagers, again if you have any stored to send.
- You can no longer "lose" a game when playing on the World Map. Instead, you lose when your entire world runs out of villagers. If you run out of villagers on a World Map game you can reset the map manually inside the world map, or send in more villagers and "take back" your land.
- The entire save system has been mostly rewritten, to allow the game to talk between save files and the world map.
- The old single map play mode has been re-purposed and named "Skirmish" mode, it functions exactly like the play mode did before the world map was introduced and is not impacted by any of the changes in this patch.
- The "Technology" button has been removed from the main menu, it will be re-added to the World Map screen once the feature has been added to the game.
- Added 4 new maps, Survival Island (new), Quiet Forest, Outlands and Enchanted Shoreline.
- Updated song "Skull Hunter"
- Removed song "Try Again", replaced with updated "Goodbye Retro-Sky"
- Added song "Azufre" and "Lonely Sunrise".

Known Issues that will be resolved before the stable build
- The new save system can introduce a heavy load to the game on initial load.
- When you run out of villagers in the world map, the game does not "End" like it should. You will have to delete your profile, or your save folder to "reset" the game.
- Lack of World Map maps, there are currently only 4. I will be adding several more before release.
- You can "cast" the "Take Resources/Creatures From Limbo" spells in game, even if Limbo is empty, wasting mana.

notes.title: Behind the scenes; Evolution of the world map.
notes.content:
Hey all! I just thought I'd give everyone a status update. It's been a while since the last patch, but development definitely has not slowed down in any way shape or form. InDev 16's new world map is one of those strange features that I can't really push like I do my normal updates.

Typically, when starting a new major update cycle I can have the first Unstable build out the door within 2 or 3 weeks, that's not the case with InDev 16. Because the world map fundamentally changes how the entire game is played it's nearly impossible to release anything until the new world map is mostly completed, luckily though we're getting close to that! I still have a lot of work left to do, but where I am now is worlds (hah!) away from where InDev 15 was a month ago when I released InDev 15i.

Most of the players who follow my twitter see my daily status updates, listing all the cool new features coming up. For those of you who don't follow me on twitter I thought I'd show you some of the progress shots to let you know what's been going on! :)

The first step was figuring out how I wanted the world map to look, this took some time, I went through several design concepts before finally settling on one. Here's a whole bunch of designs I worked through until I finally settled with the current design in production.

Design concepts:

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/mapTest1.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/worldMap4Big.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/mapTest3.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/mapTest5.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/mapTest6.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/mapTest8.png

After design after design, I finally settled down with the current version, and started to draw!

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap1.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap2.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap3.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap4.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap5.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap6.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap7.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap8.png

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/RPCMap9.png

..and finally;

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/InDev-2015-09-06-2.png

It's been a long road, I'm currently working on the GUI and save data. The biggest struggle at the moment is interconnecting all the save data together into one cohesive "world map", but progress is going great!

By Unstable 1 I expect to have the world map mostly working. By InDev 16 Stable I am planning to give the player the ability to actually bring all their maps together into one big metagame, allowing them to transfer villagers and resources from map to map using influence spells. I think this update will fundamentally change Retro-Pixel Castles, bringing it a feature very few village simulators have. I can't wait to get the update out to you guys! :)

.. oh, and by the way, the world map you see now is only about a fifth of the entire world map planned by the time Retro-Pixel Castles is released! Here's the entire map as currently planned. Each colored section is a planned map theme. :)

http://retropixelcastles.com/junk/devshots/fullMap1.png

notes.title: InDev 16 Road Map - The World Map Update
notes.content:
Well, it's that time again! I will be starting the next major update cycle for Retro-Pixel Castles. Along with the usual improvements and content as I go, I will be introducing a new major concept to the game; The World Map!

If you've been following my twitter, you've probably seen a lot of drafts for various map concepts. I've been slowly working on and planning a new map system while I've been releasing InDev 15 series content updates, and now it's time to go full force into InDev 16.

It'll be a while before InDev 16 Unstable 1 is released, the first step to begin fully implementing the world map is a redesign of the saved game system. The old system was designed to make each save encapsulated per map, the new one will have to be able to cross talk between the various maps and share data. As such, it'll take quite a bit of code to hammer out before I can start work on implementing the world map system itself into the game.

As always, all road maps are subject to change as development progresses and there will probably be a lot of delicious small additions along the way, but here are the current plans!

InDev 16 Road Map
World Map
- Brand new World Map system, when you click on "Play", instead of being taken to the map selection screen, you'll be taken to a full hand drawn world map you can scroll around on.
- Each official map pack will have it's own themed region on the map. As development progresses, more map regions will open up. Currently about a dozen are planned, many of them themes based on Kickstarter's backer rewards. InDev 16 is slated to release about 2 or 3 of these map packs.
- Instead of starting a map with a handful of random villagers, you'll instead have a pool of starting villagers you can select from each time you start a new game. When these villagers die in survival mode, they are sent back to the world map screen to be reused in other maps. 
- To get more villagers, and have enough villagers to play on multiple maps at once, you'll have to breed them while playing. 

New Save System
- Due to the world map addition, the save system will have to be rewritten nearly from scratch. This will be mostly an internal change, but will dramatically change how the save system functions.

Other Miscellaneous Changes
- The Cullis Gate mechanics will be changed, instead of spawning in a few random villagers from time to time, it'll grab random available villagers from the world map's villager pool.
- A new building or godlike ability will be added, that will allow you to "send" villagers and possibly resources out of the map and into the world map to be used to play on other maps, allowing you to pool resources in one map and send them to another new game in the future.

notes.title: Build InDev 15h Stable Released
notes.content:
It's finally here, a tips system to teach you how to play this complicated little game! You will now get tips as you play the game, trying to help you understand the world around you. These tips only pop up once per profile (not per game). Players loading up an old save may find themselves getting bombarded with tips, don't worry. It's just a side effect of you never seeing any of them before. If you're already a veteran player you can disable the tips when creating a profile, or in your settings menu.

More tips will be added, and current ones changed around or improved as development progresses.

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 15h Change Log
- Full tips system, the game will now notify you of important information as you play.
- The new tips system can be disabled in the settings menu, or when you create your profile.
- Loading screen redesigned, and now displays game tips.
- When the Banished and Recall spells are used, any mobs who were targeting a mob that was teleported will become confused when the target suddenly vanishes.
- Fixed the Black Sands map, removing a few bad spawn areas.
- Cancel Action message now displays behind the top GUI, rather than on top of it.
- Fixed a bug that would crash the game if a liquid particle went beyond the bounds of the map and tries to pool.
- Moved a male Kickstarter name from the female to the male names pool.
- Fixed an issue where some particles would continue to generate, even if the game was paused.
- Sound adjustments work again.

notes.title: Build InDev 15e Stable Released
notes.content:
This update has a few bug fixes in it, some nice memory optimizations and a lower download size. It also is the first patch to introduce the weather system to the game!

Hope you all enjoy it!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 15e Change Log
- It can now rain!
- Lightning can strike when it rains, the bolts can damage (and sometimes light on fire) the terrain, villagers, buildings or whatever else it hits.
- When raining, crops will grow faster and fires will extinguish faster.
- Villagers happiness will slowly go down if it's raining and they're outside.
- The game now supports streaming .ogg audio files, and as such the entire soundtrack has been converted to .ogg format.
- Due to the new .ogg format, music no longer has to be pre-loaded into the game lowering both ram usage and initial load times.
- Also due to the new .ogg format, the overall download size of the game has been reduced by roughly 250mb.
- Fixed a bug that would cause villagers to wander around "invisible" sometimes.

notes.title: Build InDev 15d Stable Released
notes.content:
The next content-centric patch for the InDev 15 series is here! This patch adds a bunch of food, a new map, some new terrains, and a mess of bug fixes and rebalancing.

.. oh, and mobs can swim now. ;)

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 15d Change Log
- Added map "Black Sands" to the Official Map list.
- Added a warning message if you try to load an old save game from a previous version of the game.
- Updated the minimap colors for the new terrains added in InDev 15c.
- Added depth mapping, now mobs can sink into certain terrain, like tar.
- Some terrain is now invulnerable, like water and lava for example. They can no longer be destroyed by any spells or mobs.
- Mobs can now swim across water if they feel it's the most suitable way to get to their destination.
- "Wandering" AI behavior now takes into account the movement cost to get to a tile, so they're less likely to walk into and around high cost tiles, like tar, crystals and swim in water for no reason.
- Villagers now go home to sleep when their energy is below 20, rather than 50.
- Both the chance to find a new partner, and the chance to mate with that partner have been greatly increased.
- Fire Bolt energy costs have been cut in half.
- "Motivate Land" spell now correctly displays a more accurate influence cost.
- The influence bar now highlights the amount of influence that will be consumed when you cast the currently selected spell or turns red if you lack the required influence.
- Fixed a crash if you use recall or banish on a mob and another mob is following it.
- Fixed a crash if a mob is following another mob, and suddenly the path becomes completely blocked. (Related to the above bug as well)
- New food! Cactus.
- Cactus, and all previous foods (Turnips and Potatoes) can now be planted and harvested properly, and will no longer magically become carrots instead.
- Water texture changed to be more visually suitable for swimming.
- The map editor's info panel now properly loses focus if you close the panel.

notes.title: Build InDev 15 Stable Released
notes.content:
All of the sudden, Retro-Pixel Castles feels a lot more godlike! Introducing InDev 15 Stable, the long awaited influence update.

This build is a huge landmark, introducing the groundwork to a lot of Retro-Pixel Castle's future features, and finally starting to blend elements of godlikes and village simulations together into one cohesive unit. The influence system is far from completed, this update is just the beginning, but I hope you all enjoy the great new features!

Another major change in this patch is the AI system, the entire AI system was gutted and completely rewritten from the ground up. The new AI is somewhat smarter, more dynamic and overall easier to work on. This new system will allow me to work on much more complicated behaviors in the future that will make them all feel a lot more natural. I've already added many more branches to the AI, and the unstable build testers have already reported it has been a great improvement, so I hope the rest of you enjoy it too!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 15 Change Log
- Added a the new "Influence System", that allows the player to manipulate the game world with various godlike abilities. An influence bar has been added to the top GUI, you will gain Influence (mana) based on how happy your villagers are and you can use the influence points to cast various godlike spells and abilities.
- New Spell: Fire Blast - Will rain down hellfire on the target, aim carefully!
- New Spell: Motivate Land - Will encourage natural resources to rapidly grow in the targeted area.
- New Spell: Flame - Will ignite the targets in the area on fire.
- New Spell: Dissolve - Will dissolve crystals, turning them into essence.
- New Spell: Healing Aura - Will heal all friendly villagers in the target area.
- New Spell: Distract - Will get villagers attention, making them curiously walk over to the target area. Will also do superficial damage if you accidentally hit one of them.
- New Spell: Recall - Teleports villagers or harvested resources in the target area to a safe location inside the village.
- New Spell: Banish - Teleports all the hostile monsters in the area somewhere randomly on the map. 
- Mobs can now catch on fire.
- The Fire Bolt tower will now ignite targets it hits. 
- Fixed a minor bug detecting buildings and objects in range of a mob returning incorrect values, causing mobs to ignore buildings on occasion. 
- Destroying crystal, rather than harvesting it, will now release a little bit of essence. 
- Increased the tool tip delay. 
- Completely new AI system, rewritten from scratch.
- Villagers who have no home will now attempt to sleep near buildings or walls instead of open fields.
- Villagers now only do work on the range map when building, dismantling, repairing, delivering resources. 
- Villagers can now be confused, wandering around not knowing what to do for a little while. 
- Villagers can now chat with each other when they're idle.
- Villagers now find mates by chatting with other villagers.
- Villagers who go to visit their mate will now automatically start talking to them.
- Completely rebalanced the happiness system.
- Child birth, coitus, working, being pregnant, carrying resources and many other tasks now consume additional energy and hunger.
- The effects of being stunned are now accumulative and stack.
- Lowered the maximum pack size of skeletons and zombies.
- Reduced the aggro range of all mobs.
- Optimized the combat search behavior.
- Fixed a bug where villagers were incorrectly detecting what building they were near.
- Children now attempt to live with their parents.
- When villagers look for a home they will now visit the home first before claiming it, and then go inside.
- A mob's current task is now displayed in their bottom GUI.
- A mob's current walking path is now displayed when you click on them.
- Flipped the default keys for "Brush up" and "Brush down".
- Updated map "Altaria" and added map "Loom" by Kingroka
- Added map "Captain Cal" by Primoslate
- Added maps "Ocriana" and Treacherous Lands" by Joris De Reus 
- Added the unimplemented White Rock terrain.
- Added new resource artwork to match the various terrain colors. 
- Added new graphical category tabs for the left and right GUI, replacing the old text-based ones.
- Added some particle effects to the GUI buttons. 
- Added a bunch of new mouse cursors. 
- A "pause" icon now hovers over paused buildings.
- Added a new music track, "Night is Coming" and "Hereafter Faith".
- Remastered tracks "Pixel Village", "Main Theme" and "Main Theme Piano"

- Villagers who go to visit their mate will now automatically start talking to them.
- Completely rebalanced the happiness system.
- Child birth, coitus, working, being pregnant, carrying resources and many other tasks now consume additional energy and hunger.
- The effects of being stunned are now accumulative and stack.
- Lowered the maximum pack size of skeletons and zombies.
- Reduced the aggro range of all mobs.
- Optimized the combat search behavior.
- Fixed a bug where villagers were incorrectly detecting what building they were near.

- When villagers look for a home they will now visit the home first before claiming it, and then go inside.
- Added a new music track, "Night is Coming".
- Updated map "Altaria" and added map "Loom" by Kingroka
- Added map "Captain Cal" by Primoslate

notes.title: Build InDev 14e Stable Released!
notes.content:
Surprise mini-patch! I've completed the new Drawing Board mode, I had originally I planned to release this build as InDev 15 Unstable 1 today but I realized there's no logical reason for this build to be considered unstable. So rather than adding it into the first release of the InDev 15 update series, I decided it would make more sense to release as the final part of the InDev 14 series since there are no actual game play changes and as such it is a pretty stable build, so here it is! 

You can now access a live-updated list of upcoming features for RPC by simply clicking the "Drawing Board" button on the main menu. Drawing Board mode will connect to the internet and load a copy of the latest official drawing board for you to view, whenever you're curious to see the latest official list of confirmed features you can quickly and easily check it out right in the game. This list will be constantly updated, so be sure to check it out regularly if you're the curious type. :)

Enjoy!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 14e Mini-Patch Change Log
- Drawing Board mode! View the latest copy of the official planned features list with a simple button click.
- Removed the Statistics button to make room for the new Drawing Board button. The Statistics button will be re-added once the statistics section is completed.

notes.title: Build InDev 14d Stable Released!
notes.content:
InDev 14d is out, this mini-patch's main focus was to add the heavily requested Clear Terrain function to the game and throw in a bunch of tweaks and bug fixes before starting in on the next big patch.

Warning!: One of the changes in this patch greatly increases the base stats of all mobs across the board, meaning old save files will be completely crippled. Sadly this means your villagers will probably find themselves barely able to move due to the new movement speed calculations being based on the new stat system, and they'll be slaughtered very quickly by the first newly spawned mob that attacks the village. I highly recommend starting a new game!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 14d Mini-Patch Change Log
- Clear Terrain tool added, you can now assign terrain to be completely obliterated by your builders, but the process will not return any resources.
- Reduced the Fire Bolt tower costs from 15 energy to 10.
- Villagers are much more willing to flee when outside the village.
- Mobs now reconsider their combat targets when they are hit, occasionally turning around and attacking their attacker even if they already have a target they are chasing.
- All mob stats have been increased across the board.
- Pregnancy chances have been increased slightly.
- Fixed stone shack description.
- Fixed a loading crash when some particles wouldn't load correctly.
- Greatly increased monster aggression, they will almost never run away anymore.
- Alerting other villagers of an attack will no longer occasionally pull the entire villager.
- Tweaked the selection dot graphics a bit.
- Total housing is now displayed in the top GUI, instead of total buildings.
- Monsters now gain much less experience burrowing through terrain.
- "Total Heroes" added to the population tab.
- Ghosts can no longer be selected when they're invisible.
- Fixed a bug that would allow adults to couple with children (Eww, I know right?) that could eventually crash the game under very specific conditions.
- Tweaked the mini-tutorial overlay on the village center.
- Combat AI now disables if the mob is "stuck" (standing on a blocked tile), preventing a AI related crash.
- Slightly increased all villagers movement speed.
- Can no longer build on any rough terrain of any kind. You need to clear it first!

notes.title: InDev 15 - The Influence Update - Road Map.
notes.content:
It's time to get crack'in on the next update, InDev 15!

InDev 15's major focus will be the new influence system. In a nutshell, this update is all about finally adding the long awaited "God like" features to our little simulation. :)

Why only one planned feature? Well, it's pretty simple. I try to find a good balance of features to add from build to build, my main goal when I plan the next major update is to try to keep each update about a month apart. (InDev 14 broke the mold, taking two months!)

The Influence System may sound fairly simple to add on paper, it'll require a bunch of foundational code. I want to make sure I don't get locked into adding too much at once before I can get another stable build shipped out to you guys, and since the entire system seems pretty encapsulated (AKA: It shouldn't have much of a major effect on the rest of the game's code) it just seems ideal to focus on it alone, while doing my usual optimizing, bug fixes and working on fan-generated ideas and suggestions on the side as I go.

InDev 14 Road Map
Influence System
The major addition to InDev 15 will be the influence system. As currently planned, the influence system will be a new tab added to the work tab on the left hand side. When selected you'll have various "godly" influence command you can use to manipulate the environment. These abilities will not be unlimited though, you'll slowly gain influence points as you play based on how many villagers you have and how happy they are. The overall purpose of the system is to bring a little more "god like" elements into the simulation.

Some examples of what the influence system will be used for;
- Scare villagers and monsters.
- Resurrect ghosts and corpses.
- Zap a monster with a fire bolt or twelve.
- Regrow a small chunk of trees.
- Heal a group of villagers.
- Spawn in extra essence.

notes.title: Build InDev 14b Stable Released!
notes.content:
After over two months of development, the game changing InDev 14 is here! 

InDev 14 features a ton of new systems, optimizations and general improvements. The two major additions are the new guards, heroes, and the first half of the plans for building destruction. The patch also comes with a new pathfinding system, lighting system, improved particle rendering, more AI improvements, more buildings, and even ghosts!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 14b HOTFIX Change Log
 - Fixed the female villager names in the bottom pop out GUI for the building worker lists. They were incorrectly formatting the name and cutting off the first character.
 - Fixed a bug causing the tutorial messages in the play mode from not popping up.
 - Added a link to the new mini-guide on the disclaimer page.
 - Game now starts windowed by default.

InDev 14 Change Log
- Buildings can now be attacked, destroyed, catch on fire and be repaired.
- If you wall your village in, monsters will attempt to dig a hole through the terrain or tear down walls to reach you.
- Builders can now repair buildings and put out fires.
- New map AI system. Now trees, food and crystals can slowly regrow and expand on the map.
- The Crystal Motivator. A new building that can be built near crystal beds to encourage growth.
- New guard buildings of various sizes, once built you can assign villagers to them and they will do their best to protect your village from invaders.
- The hero system. When a villager is created they have a small chance to become a hero, heroes are similar to guards. They will wander around the village defending it. Heroes can not be assigned any jobs, but have extremely high boosted stats. All villages start with at least one hero.
- Ghosts! Now, sometimes you'll be visited by your dead comrades at night.
- The harvest buttons on the work tab hide if you have no way to harvest anything of that type. For example, the harvest crystals button will be hidden until a Crystillery is built.
- New console added that displays basic messages, like when villagers die, are attacked or level up.
- Rewrote the font coloring system, and as such, many of the font colors have changed.
- Fixed spacing glitch in text boxes when the last character of a string was a space.
- Completely rewritten A* Pathfinding, pathfinding is more natural and now accounts for movement speeds on certain terrain that has a movement penalty.
- Walking on crystals and food now slow down the villager slightly.
- Removed the "Decorative" and "Flooring" object categories, will be readded once something is put inside them.
- Renamed the "Tower" category to "Defense".
- Added a basic mouse cursor and gave it some basic particle effects.
- Doubled the amount of blood!
- You can now "Interact" with monsters on the main menu.
- Skeletons and Slimes now spawn on the main menu.
- Blood particle splatters now go in the direction the target was hit, not the opposite direction he was facing.
- Reduced the frequency Kickstarter names are used on regular villagers, but they're now always used for heroes.
- Added "Dust" particles for many tasks.
- Mobs now run to/away from their targets, leaving a smoke trail behind them.
- Dismantling now has the same sound effects as building.
- Villagers can now alert other villagers around them when they are being attacked.
- The clock dial is now animated.
- You can now pause the game by clicking on the clock.
- Rewrote the lighting system, it now renders faster, uses less memory and generates more round shaped light patterns.
- Essence has been optimized, and now a single essence can have more than 1 energy value. High energy essence is larger, with a glowing red center.
- Tweaked fight and flight mechanics. (That's right, again!)
- Villagers can now find mates, go their mates and breed even if they are not idle.
- Essence Collector regeneration speed reduced by 50%.
- Optimized tower and mob target searching mechanics.
- Villagers have a short delay before they can mate or get pregnant again.
- Villagers can now have twins or triplets.
- All mob health increased greatly.
- Fire tower firing speed reduced, but the damage has been increased.
- Eating food now restores 20% of the mob's maximum hunger, instead of just 20 points.
- Food heals 10% of the mob's health.
- Villagers will now go home to recover health if their health drops too low.
- Lowered the maximum pack size of zombies and skeletons from 24 to 8.
- Removed the hitbox links from the main menu.
- Removed the tutorial link from the disclaimer page.
- Improved the particle rendering speed by about 20-30% on most modern machines.
- Fixed a bug where children were not spawning with their parent's last name.
- Fixed a bug where the Cullis Gate would spawn in "0 to 2" villagers when it should be spawning in "1 to 3", thus sometimes making the Cullis Gate do absolutely nothing when it fires.
- Fixed a bug that would cause some worker actions to crash the game.
- Fixed a bug causing the combat AI to "dance diagonally back and forth" when two mobs were attacking each other.
- Crops are now correctly removed from a building when it is destroyed or dismantled.
- Fixed a crash if you clicked on a blank spot on the villager list.
- Fixed a internal bug that would refresh an objects tiles more often than needed.
- Fixed a bug where creating a new map in the map editor would set the view port out in the middle of space.
- and as always, tons of small optimizations and bug fixes.

notes.title: Build InDev 14 Unstable 6 Released
notes.content:
Click here for help on accessing the Unstable branch!

The game changer, InDev 14 Unstable 6 has been released! This is the first ever release of Retro-Pixel Castles that has building destruction! That's right, the days of walling yourself in with your invulnerable walls are over! This is also a near-stable release, so get cracking on those bugs, we should be seeing InDev 14 Stable very soon!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 14 Unstable 6 Change Log
- Buildings and walls can all be attacked, catch fire, repaired and destroyed.
- Terrain can all be attacked and destroyed.
- Builders can now repair buildings and put out fires.
- Monsters will now search for an unblocked path to get to your village, if none is found they will find the shortest path through topography and walls, destroying whatever is in their path. (Hint: Don't completely wall yourself in!)
- Screen shake added, your screen will shake whenever monsters attack your buildings.
- Added billowing smoke cloud particles.
- Added explosion particles.
- Added 3 new guard buildings, villagers assigned to these buildings will share similar mechanics as heroes and defend the village if anyone or anything is attacked.
- Fixed a minor glitch in the Small Crystillery's particle generation.
- Particles can now be rendered on top of mobs.
- Villagers now heal when they are in their home, and go home to regenerate if their health drops too low.
- All mobs now fully heal when they level up.
- All mobs now have much more health.
- Eating food now restores 20% of a mob's hunger instead of a fixed amount, and also heals the mob by 10%.
- Game no longer starts paused when you load a new game after losing.
- Fixed a very rare crash when a mob would attempt to flee after being spawned on a blocked tile.
- Added all the new GUI artwork for the Guard buildings and Crystal Motivator.

notes.title: InDev 14 - The Influence and Heroes Update - Road Map.
notes.content:
Coming soon to a Retro-Pixel Castles near you, a few new systems that I think will really add to the depth and complexity of the game play. The influence system, heroes and building/wall damage.

As always, more content than whats on the road map will be added along with the usual bug fixes. These are just the primary goals of the update. There's also a few things originally planned for InDev 13 that didn't quite make it in, that I plan to get into 14.

InDev 14 Road Map
Influence System
- One of the more interesting features of InDev 14 will be the influence system. As currently planned, the influence system will be a new tab added to the work tab on the left hand side, when selected you'll have various "godly" influence command you can use to manipulate the environment. For example, you could scare or lure villagers around, maybe zap a monster with lightning, or regrow a small chunk of trees. 

These influences will cost "Influence" points that will be slowly generated as you play the game, and the rate these points are accumulated will be based on your village's average happiness.

Heroes
- This will be the first update to introduce hero class villagers to the game. The first heroes added will just be your basic fighters, they will be born/summoned randomly from time to time. For the most part they will act like normal villagers, but with a couple of major differences. First, they will never be allowed to be assigned to buildings at all. Second, they will have boosted stats, and third they will roam around your village protecting your villagers and slaying nearby monsters on their own. For example, some expected AI you'll see is heroes patrolling the village killing off near by monsters, and running to protect villagers, buildings and resources that are attacked.

Building and Wall Damage
- Finally, monsters will be able to damage your pretty things. This means if you try to wall yourselves in, the bad guys are just going to start tearing down your walls!

It's important to note though, that while the monsters will be able to tear down walls and knock over buildings, they will usually try to take the shortest non-blocked path to your village. You can use this to your advantage to bottleneck them into a pit of towers, but if you wall yourself in completely, all bets are off!

notes.title: Build InDev 13b Stable Released!
notes.content:
InDev 13 is here! This new stable build introduces a ton of new content, tweaks, a better GUI, smaller (but much less resource intensive) maps and many other features. 

Originally it was going to be even beefier, but I've decided to push some of InDev 13's planned features into InDev 14 so as not to keep you guys from receiving an update for a while. Don't worry, there are no delays. The content you will be getting in 14 you would of gotten around the same time anyway, I just decided to break up InDev 13 into two updates so you can get some of the features a little early. :)

So, I hope you enjoy the new features! 

IMPORTANT NOTE: This build WILL break all your previous custom maps. You must use the map converter found in the Retro-Pixel Castles install folder to continue using them!

You can report bugs over at the official website's Support and Bugs Forum, or on the Steam Discussion Board. :)

InDev 13b HOTFIX Change Log
- Fixed issue with OSX not reading text files correctly, causing the game to crash.
- Fixed credits roll being blank on OSX.

InDev 13 Change Log
- New 256x256 map size.
- Added a console based map converter, to convert your maps from the old 512x512 to the new 256x256 system. It can be found in the Retro-Pixel Castles install folder.
- Due to the decreased map size, frame rate, memory usage, and system requirements have dropped dramatically. 
- Added new "Wheat Wind" track.
- Converted "The Quiet Forest" and "Hunted" into 8 smaller maps.
- Removed all of the Developer's Choice Maps, except the ones that were originally "Small" or "Medium" sized maps. (Others will be re-added once the authors convert them to their liking.)
- Added a bunch of new tile sets; Sandstone (In Red, Black and Tan), new Rock (in Black, Brown, Red and White).
- Added two new foods, Turnips and Potatoes. But they currently still think they're carrots.
- New map tiles property loader, that helps decrease load time.
- Fixed a bug where sometimes walls would not connect together correctly.
- Drawing in the map editor now no longer replaces the same tile if it already exists.
- Main Menu now loads random maps from the Official Maps pack.
- Added a "Recent News and Announcements" box on the main menu.
- "Stone" resources renamed to "Rock".
- New resources: Boards (Refined logs), Stone (Refined rock) and Crylithium (Refined Crystals).
- Harvesting buildings can now refine the resources brought in into the new refined resources listed above. For example, the Lumber Mill will manufacture boards, and the Crystillery will manufacture Crylithium.
- Completely rebalanced all the building requirements. Many advanced buildings require the new refined resources.
- Added the Small and Regular Crystillary, used for harvesting crystals.
- Added the Cullis Gate, a large Essence Collector like building that will build up and discharge large amounts of energy attempting to summon new villagers into the game ... or other things.
- Rebalanced many of the building costs, and magic based buildings like the Essence Collector and Fire Bolt tower now require crystals to be built.
- Added some new particle effects to the game to use with the new Cullis Gate.
- Added some blue fire flickers to the Essence Collector.
- Essence Collectors and Fire Bolt towers no longer generate essence.
- Essence Collectors and the new Cullis Gate are now fueled with Crylithium.
- Essence Collector's maximum energy reduced to 250.
- Re-added the "Category" frame icons to the Play and Map Editor GUIs.
- Added a pause button for buildings.
- Completely redrawn the bottom pop out GUI in the play mode.
- Completely recoded and redrawn the population tab. The new population tab now lists how many villagers are not employed, homeless, have a mate, or are pregnant along with some other miscellaneous information.
- Added a new buildings tab, based off the new populations tab. The new building tab lists how much total housing you have, how many total workers you have and many other useful tidbits.
- You can click on buildings or villagers in either of the two new tabs to center on them. (Note: Currently, in low resolutions sometimes the center may be under the GUI)
- Many miscellaneous GUI artwork improvements.
- New Mob: The Skeleton. They do not have much health, or hit hard. But they're extremely fast and can sometimes run past your towers.
- Lowered the monster spawn rate substantially.
- Fixed a bug in the map editor's info panel that would not detect if you're trying to use a map name already taken.
- Moved the resource bar in the play mode to above the top GUI.
- Removed the water sparkle trail from Essence.
- Added a new objects tab, when you select an object to build in play mode a small description of that object and the requirements to build it will be displayed.
- Fixed a bug that was causing lag when looking for resources on ground.
- Fixed a bug where villagers would pick up resources to use they shouldn't need, and set them back on the ground.
- Added the Kickstarter Backer's names to the villager name pool.
- Updated the Credits page, adding the additional Kickstarter Backers who submitted their surveys late.
- Added all the Kickstarter Backer's quotes to the game.
- Fixed the lag some users experienced in the credits page.
- Fixed a localization issue that would cause some user's copy of the game to crash attempting to find game resources (Thanks to: khadgar.rumnheim for finding the solution!)
- Tons of under the hood code cleanup.

notes.title: Build InDev 13b Stable Released!
notes.content:

Originally it was going to be even beefier, but I've decided to push some of InDev 13's planned features into InDev 14 so as not to keep you guys from receiving an update for a while. Don't worry, there are no delays. The content you will be getting in 14 you would of gotten around the same time anyway, I just decided to break up InDev 13 into two updates so you can get some of the features a little early. :)

So, I hope you enjoy the new features! 

IMPORTANT NOTE: This build WILL break all your previous custom maps. You must use the map converter found in the Retro-Pixel Castles install folder to continue using them!

notes.title: Backwards compatibility during Early Access - Seeking input.
notes.content:
CLICK HERE TO VOTE IN THE POLL

There is a tough decision I have to make currently sitting on my plate, and I want your guy's input before I make it, because you're all the ones being effected by it! During the development of InDev 13 I've come to realize something; Making the game backwards compatible with old InDev builds is a pain, and very time consuming.

Making sure people keep their user generated content is extremely important to me, I remember many times in my gaming life that I've lost all my hard work. A save file for Baldur's Gate, a cool Quake II skin, a Starcraft map, a mod for a Duke Nukem, even some Minecraft worlds I've lost over the years. I hate to lose things I've worked so hard on, and I would hate it even more to force others to lose things too.

Well because of that, I decided I would dedicate a lot of my time in Retro-Pixel Castle's development making sure the game was always as backwards compatible as I could possibly make it so you guys would lose as little content as possible. The problem is I've come to realize during my work on InDev 13 that maybe that's not the best idea this early in development. I am spending quite a lot of time every update making sure content from previous InDev versions still work because while we're in InDev, I make many fundamental changes to the core code. If I could recover the time spent focusing on making the game backwards compatible, I could get RPC released much earlier.

I have no problem making the game backwards compatible, but I think for the greater good of development I shouldn't worry about it until we reach late alpha, or beta. But since this is something important to you guys, I'm putting it up for a vote!

Option 1: Don't worry about backwards compatibility during InDev and Alpha, unless it's something simple to add.
Pro:
- Faster development, thus more content and a earlier release date.
Con:
- All save files, custom maps, and other content could break between updates. (Although I will avoid this as much as possible, and will write converters if it isn't too time consuming.)
 
Option 2: Try everything in my power to make the game as backwards compatible as possible, even if the game takes longer to develop.
Pro:
- You guys will (most of the time) get to keep your save games, and your custom maps with a few rare exceptions.
Cons:
- Development time may be much longer. Could even tack on months of additional dev time, because I have to carefully code things keeping old content in mind, and will sometimes have to code custom content converters (Like the map converter that is currently bundled in InDev 13 Unstable 1).
- Sometimes development may seem "messy" as I have to bandaid in ways to convert content. The map converter is a good example of this, because it's already needing tweaked for the upcoming Unstable 2 release.
- At least during InDev, sometimes your content may have to be broken anyway.
 
So please, give me your input on this and vote in the poll.

A save file for Baldur's Gate, a cool Quake II skin, a Starcraft map, a mod for a Duke Nukem, even some Minecraft worlds I've lost over the years. I hate to lose things I've worked so hard on, and I would hate it even more to force others to lose things too.

Well because of that, I decided I would dedicate a lot of my time in Retro-Pixel Castle's development making sure the game was always as backwards compatible as I could possibly make it so you guys would lose as little content as possible. The problem is I've come to realize during my work on InDev 13 that maybe that's not the best idea this early in development. I am spending quite a lot of time every update making sure content from previous InDev versions still work because while we're in InDev, I make many fundamental changes to the core code. If I could recover the time spent focusing on making the game backwards compatible, I could get RPC released much earlier.

I have no problem making the game backwards compatible, but I think for the greater good of development I shouldn't worry about it until we reach late alpha, or beta. But since this is something important to you guys, I'm putting it up for a vote!

Option 1: Don't worry about backwards compatibility during InDev and Alpha, unless it's something simple to add.
Pro:
- Faster development, thus more content and a earlier release date.
Con:
- All save files, custom maps, and other content could break between updates. (Although I will avoid this as much as possible, and will write converters if it isn't too time consuming.)
 
Option 2: Try everything in my power to make the game as backwards compatible as possible, even if the game takes longer to develop.
Pro:
- You guys will (most of the time) get to keep your save games, and your custom maps with a few rare exceptions.
Cons:
- Development time may be much longer. Could even tack on months of additional dev time, because I have to carefully code things keeping old content in mind, and will sometimes have to code custom content converters (Like the map converter that is currently bundled in InDev 13 Unstable 1).
- Sometimes development may seem "messy" as I have to bandaid in ways to convert content. The map converter is a good example of this, because it's already needing tweaked for the upcoming Unstable 2 release.
- At least during InDev, sometimes your content may have to be broken anyway.
 
So please, give me your input on this and vote in the poll.
